card.stem: A dwelling house has a 400 mm concrete block wall with a full-fill insulated cavity supported on a traditional strip foundation. The wall is plastered on both sides. The insulated concrete ground floor is finished with 20 mm floor tiles as shown.
card.questionText: To a scale of 1:5, draw a vertical section through the strip foundation, external wall and ground floor. On your drawing show the typical construction details from the bottom of the foundation to a point 200 mm above finished floor level. Show an internal floor width of 900 mm and include four typical dimensions.

rows.contextNote: Credit the best SEVEN acceptable details at 5 marks each, capped at 35. Marked details: reinforced strip foundation 1200 × 400 mm; concrete fill / foundation blocks; hardcore and sand blinding; 1200-gauge DPC/radon barrier; 200–300 mm floor insulation; 150 mm concrete floor slab taped and sealed at the wall junction; 20 mm floor tiles; skirting board; block inner leaf with 13 mm plaster; 200 mm full-fill cavity insulation; wall ties; block outer leaf with 19 mm render.
Four appropriate typical dimensions on the section.

rows.verbatim: Draughting, accuracy and scale (excellent, good, fair)
rows.contextNote: Draughting, accuracy and scale of the section: excellent 8, good 6, fair 4.

card.questionText: A wood-burning stove can be used to heat radiators for a dwelling house. Draw a large freehand sketch of the given house and, on your sketch, show the pipework necessary to supply hot water from the stove to the ground floor radiators and also heat the water in the cylinder on the first floor. Include the following in your sketch: wood-burning stove; hot water cylinder; pipework to cylinder; expansion tank / vessel; pipework to radiators; all necessary pumps and valves.

rows.contextNote: Credit the best EIGHT acceptable items at 5 marks each, capped at 40. Marked items: drawing the given sketch; 15 mm cold feed to the burner; 22 mm flow to the radiators; 22 mm return from the radiators; radiators; 22 mm primary flow to the cylinder; 22 mm primary return to the burner; 22 mm overflow pipe; 22 mm expansion pipe from the cylinder; valves / pumps.
Quality of the sketch: excellent 6, good 4, fair 2.

card.stem: Careful planning is required to manage waste on a construction site so as to reduce, re-use and recycle construction materials. The sketch shows one possible waste management method used to sort materials on a site.
card.questionText: Discuss two reasons why a construction company should have a waste management plan for their site.

rows.contextNote: Such as: to prevent and minimise waste on building sites; to build a culture of re-using and recycling rather than dumping.

A second, different reason. Such as: less energy used making new material; a clean, clear site that prevents accidents; hazardous waste kept out of local water supplies; landfill sites are scarce; a lower overall building cost.

card.questionText: Using large freehand sketches, show three safety signs highlighting the use of personal protection equipment (PPE) that must be worn by all workers on a construction site. For each sign, state how the personal protection equipment protects workers on the site.

rows.contextNote: Sign 6 and how it protects the worker 2 (the scheme’s "Safety sign 1" and "Reason 1"). Such as: steel toe cap boots (feet protected from dropped heavy materials); hi-viz clothing (workers visible to machine operators); hard hat (head protected from falling material); protective eye wear (eyes protected from debris, dust and power tools); ear protection (continuous noise of 85–90 dB or more); hand protection (sharp equipment, corrosive or toxic substances).

card.questionText: Explain, with the aid of notes and freehand sketches, any five of the following: stud partition; domino joint; slump test; dynamic glass; pyrite; pile foundation; trimmer; butt hinge; solar panel.

rows.contextNote: Explain any five of the nine terms. Each term is marked separately: primary communication of relevant information 6 and other communication 4, in notes or sketches (the scheme reserves no fixed split between them). Stud partition: a timber or metal stud frame fixed to the floor, ceiling and walls; vertical studs at 400 mm centres between head and sole plates, braced by noggins and covered with plasterboard; load bearing or non-load bearing. Domino joint: a woodworking joint cut with a domino joiner, used in modern furniture to butt, edge or corner join pieces of wood quickly; very strong with wood adhesive. Slump test: measures the workability of fresh concrete on site, batch by batch, and checks the water content; a truncated cone, tamping rod and meter stick; 0–50 mm slump low workability, 50–75 mm medium. Dynamic glass: a thin coating that changes from clear to tinted under a small DC voltage (electrochromic) or with the sun’s heat (thermochromic), reducing glare and overheating for the occupants’ comfort. Pyrite: a naturally occurring iron sulphide in sedimentary rock that cracks and expands when exposed to moisture and oxygen; in fill under a building it heaves ground floors and cracks walls. Pile foundation: supports and anchors a building where the soil has low bearing capacity or good soil is deep; end-bearing, friction or short-bored, drilled and poured or driven; a ground beam carries the walls onto the piles. Trimmer: a joist supporting the ends of trimmed joists or rafters around a stairwell or chimney opening, carried by trimming joists; carries more load, so usually 25 mm thicker than common joists. Butt hinge: a widely used hinge of two leaves and a central pin, 12–150 mm long, in brass, mild steel or stainless steel; the leaves sit in shallow trenches and are fixed with countersunk screws; for doors, windows and boxes. Solar Panel: evacuated tubes converting solar radiation to heat, or photovoltaic panels generating electricity; best on a south-facing roof at about 45° in Ireland; a sustainable source that cuts CO2 emissions.
